newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta bourse blue-chips end down.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta bourse blue-chips end down.

text.p: Calcutta shares on Wednesday ended lower after failing to hold onto initial gains in the face of strong profit-taking at higher levels, brokers said.
They said that speculative activities in scrips like ITC fizzled out, dragging down prices and lowering sentiment.
Foreign investors neither sold nor bought any significant quantities resulting in a marginal fall in volumes.

"I see a short-term rally but with foreign funds showing marginal interest to invest afresh, such a rally will not sustain. Besides Indian mutual funds are booking profits at each rise and this will prevent blue-chips from stabilising at higher levels," said a dealer with brokers C. Mackertich.
"Besides, with the festive season ahead and bourses slated to go on holiday most speculative buyers would prefer to square up positions. This is pulling down prices," he said.
